seed: Shannon Byrne Susko, Master Deck with 2 Day Kick Off, November 2024, Metronomics.

slides.title: A winning team needs a shared way to work.
slides.headline: A winning team needs a shared way to work.
notes: Keep the overview brief. Metronomics connects the team, strategy, execution and cash. The workshop starts putting that shared way of working into practice.

On the Coach card, explain your role: guide the method, challenge assumptions and reveal blind spots. The team owns the plan; the CEO and leaders make the business decisions and own their commitments.

panels.heading: A repeatable system
panels.support: A common way to build and execute the plan.

panels.heading: A visible scoreboard
panels.support: The team can see the plan and its progress.

panels.heading: An outside perspective
panels.support: Challenge assumptions and uncover blind spots.

slides.title: The team and the plan must develop together.
slides.headline: The team and the plan must develop together.
notes: Three systems build the team. Three systems run the business. Develop both together; people work is not a warm-up to the real work.

panels.heading: Cohesive
panels.support: Trust, constructive conflict and commitment to team results.

panels.heading: Cultural
panels.support: Shared purpose, values and long-term ambition.

panels.heading: Strategy
panels.support: Where we will compete and how we will achieve our goals.

panels.heading: Execution
panels.support: Owned priorities, visible measures and a meeting rhythm.

panels.heading: Cash
panels.support: Understand cash needs and forecast through widgets.

slides.title: What could limit your growth?
slides.headline: What could limit your growth?

panels.heading: Leadership capacity
panels.support: Can leaders grow the team as the business grows?

panels.heading: Market expertise
panels.support: Do you understand the market you intend to serve?

panels.heading: Scalable infrastructure and processes
panels.support: Can your systems support the next stage of growth?

notes: Shannon names leadership, market expertise, and scalable infrastructure and process as growth constraints.
Ask which constraint the team sees today. Use this to frame the following readiness diagnosis.

slides.title: Growth builds on the foundation.
slides.headline: Growth builds on the foundation.
notes: These are readiness conditions, not guaranteed calendar stages. Teams can move backward as conditions change.
Connect A-player to the later question: would you fight to keep each member of your team?
Momentum adds Team Trust 2.0, validated strategy and Coach Cascade turned on. Compounding sustains these with Coach Cascade flowing.

Ask out loud, no slide: Is your cash system working? Does execution work without you? Would you fight to keep everyone on your team? Do you have a clear, mapped strategy? A no marks unfinished foundation work, not a grade.

panels.heading: Foundation
panels.support: Working cash and execution; an A-player, cohesive leadership team; mapped strategy.

panels.heading: Momentum
panels.support: Keep the foundation. Validate strategy, deepen trust and begin coaching others.

panels.heading: Compounding
panels.support: Sustain the systems. Coaching flows throughout the organization.

slides.title: Teams learn to work through disagreement.
slides.headline: Teams learn to work through disagreement.
notes: Shannon connects the growth phases to Bruce Tuckman’s team-development model.
Do not promise a linear path or equate disagreement with failure. Healthy conflict helps build commitment.
Close by asking: does the leadership team put team results first?
Invite leaders to describe current behavior rather than give a polished answer.
What would need to change for the whole team to own the outcome?
Leaders develop from doing expert work themselves to coaching others who own team results. This develops over time.

panels.heading: Forming and storming
panels.support: Build trust and learn to raise difficult issues.

panels.heading: Performing
panels.support: Work together effectively toward shared results.
